summary: Riley's own parallel session must never hint or tripwire Riley (self-exclusion), and a denylisted hot file stays silent on the reader side even though a teammate context targets it server-side (as a legacy or hostile connector could plant).

workContexts.title: Payment capture retries double charge the ledger

claims.body: A retried capture posts the same charge twice to the ledger
The capture retry path skips the idempotency check that the first attempt performs

probes.prompt: payment capture retries double charging the ledger
probes.rationale: Self-exclusion on the prompt path: the reader's own parallel-session context is excluded inside the hub's search WHERE, so their own evidence-backed finding never comes back at them as a hint.
Self-session exclusion (DESIGN.md 4): a developer's own sessions and worktrees never trip their own wire — the exclusion is the hub's developer-id filter, not client-side.

Hot-file denylist: bun.lock matches **/*.lock, so the hook stays silent before any hub call — even though a teammate context really targets it hub-side, planted here exactly to prove the reader-side gate is what silences it.
